The image shows a corn ear with:
- Tip rot affecting the top portion of the ear
- Brown/discolored kernels concentrated at the tip
- White/gray mold growth visible between kernels
- Shrunken, rotted kernels at the tip with some kernel cracking
- Healthy yellow kernels on the lower portion of the ear

Key features: tip-focused kernel rot with visible whitish-gray mycelium, brownish discoloration, and kernel shriveling. This pattern is characteristic of Gibberella ear rot, which typically starts at the silk end (tip) of the ear and moves downward, with pinkish-to-white mold and kernel discoloration. The white/gray fungal growth and tip-down progression fits Gibberella well. Fusarium ear rot can look similar but often has a more pink/salmon coloration and is more scattered; Gibberella tends to be at the tip with whitish-gray to reddish mold. The visible white mycelial growth and tip rot pattern here aligns most closely with Gibberella.
